title: Energy release without a perpetual-motion cycle
promptMarkdown: A specified hypothetical fusion reaction has a mass deficit $4.0\times10^{-29}\,\mathrm{kg}$ per event, using a consistent mass convention. Calculate Q in joules and MeV, and ideal power at $2.0\times10^{14}$ events/s. Use $c=299792458\,\mathrm{m/s}$ and $1\,\mathrm{eV}=1.602176634\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm J$. At 25%conversion efficiency, calculate electrical output. Explain why reversing the reaction cannot release the same Q again, and distinguish this rest-mass budget from a guarantee that an incident fixed-target projectile needs only Q to initiate a reaction.
hintLadder: Multiply the stated mass deficit by $c^2$ before converting units.
Power is energy per event times events per second; efficiency multiplies that power.
Write the reversed mass difference and remember the target-recoil example.
